summary: Unexpected spike in 5xx errors as API gateway queues grow during GPU driver recovery and runtime reconnect storm
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 at ~02:15 UTC we observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses returned by the hosted API (primarily 502/503). The spike coincided with a cluster-level GPU driver auto-recovery event; multiple serving-runtime pods issued reconnects within a short window. Impact: Customer-facing errors for tenants on Dedicated capacity (notably NimbleDocs) with elevated request failures and higher tail latency. Intermittent streaming session disconnects were reported and some long-running requests returned 502 after upstream reset. Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated GPU pool for tenant NimbleDocs, autoscaler configured with warmup delay. Steps to reproduce: Non-deterministic; reproduced only by inducing GPU driver reset on a node while driving sustained tenant traffic (~120 QPS sustained with many long prompts). Observed behavior: API gateway acceptor queue length climbed, connection handoff latency increased, and the gateway returned 502/503 when upstream connection attempts timed out or were refused. Serving runtime logs show repeated GPU driver reset messages and a flurry of runtime restarts/reconnects. Observed correlated metrics: pod restart spike, connection_attempts/sec increase, accept_queue_depth surge, and API gateway upstream_unhealthy_count increase. Initial mitigation: throttled tenant to 30% of baseline, applied temporary per-tenant connection limit and enabled a legacy model variant to reduce GPU memory pressure. Investigation continues.
investigation_notes: 02:20 UTC - Support triage: confirmed customer errors and gathered logs from apigw and runtime.
02:33 UTC - SRE: observed driver reset traces in /var/log/nvidia* on three nodes; runtimes re-registered within seconds.

03:10 UTC - Hypothesis: simultaneous reconnects caused an acceptor-queue fanup at API gateway and a thundering reconnection behavior in the runtime health-checks, exposing a window where upstreams were temporarily unavailable.
03:45 UTC - Observed that autoscaler warmup caused new pods to attempt model load while reconnect pressure remained high, amplifying GPU memory contention.
04:12 UTC - Reproduced locally by inducing driver reset on a test node under sustained QPS; same acceptor queue growth pattern observed.

Suggested mitigations: add randomized backoff to runtime reconnects, increase apigw upstream connection backlog and add per-source conn limits, tune autoscaler warmup to stagger model reloads, and add short-lived circuit-breaker at apigw for noisy tenants.
comments: Support (Aisha): 'Customer reports elevated 5xx starting ~02:15 UTC. Collecting logs and escalation requested. Tenant NimbleDocs affected; they reported write failures in production.'

SRE (Marco): 'Confirmed driver reset events on nodes node-54, node-76, node-81. Runtimes did a rapid reconnect flood — pushing apigw acceptor queues to saturation. Implemented temporary tenant throttling and pinned NimbleDocs to legacy variant to reduce memory pressure.'

Customer (NimbleDocs - Samir Rao): 'We saw a large number of 502s and some streaming sessions disconnect. Throttling reduced errors but traffic still degraded. Please keep us updated on root cause and ETA for full fix.'
Eng (Jade Thompson): 'Adding jitter to reconnect logic and adding an acceptor-queue alert threshold as follow-up work. Raising a PR to add runtime reconnect backoff.'
SRE (Marco): 'Applied short-term gateway tuning to increase upstream_backlog and enabled circuit breaker for noisy tenant. Monitoring for improvement.'
resolution: Workaround applied: temporary per-tenant throttle and pinned model variant for NimbleDocs; apigw backlog increased and tenant circuit-breaker enabled. Long-term remediation work: add randomized reconnect backoff in runtime, staggered autoscaler warmup, and a gateway-level rate-limiter per-tenant. Engineering PRs opened; scheduling postmortem and runbook updates.
next_steps: Merge runtime reconnect-backoff PR and release canary to staging (assigned: Jade Thompson)
Update autoscaler warmup logic to stagger model loads (assigned: Infra Team)
Create apigw playbook entry for acceptor-queue growth and per-tenant circuit breaker thresholds (assigned: SRE)
Postmortem scheduled and notify affected customers with RCA (owner: Support Manager)
